

In this first section, we provide an overview of the dominant approach to causal inference in epidemiology. 

*Learning goals for this section include*:  
- Practice using NPSEMs, DAGs, and SWIGs as descriptions of the entire sample rather than an observation within a sample.  
- Practice thinking about “independence” as a combination of “no interference” and “no spillover.”  
- Practice saying “FFRCISTG” out loud.

*After reading this, you should be able to*:  
- Write an NPSEM of the whole sample based on a DAG.  
- Draw a DAG of the sample based on an NPSEM.  
- Write a causal model based on a DAG and intervention regime.  
- Draw a SWIG based on a DAG and intervention regime.  
- Apply the assumptions of FFRCISTG to a DAG or SWIG.
